CYP2D6.label: CYP2D6 (ultrarapid metabolizer)
CYP2D6.risk_type: Overdose risk — drug converted to active form too fast
CYP2D6.mechanism: Ultrarapid CYP2D6 metabolizers convert certain prodrugs into their active form far faster than normal, pushing active-drug levels to toxic concentrations even at a standard dose.
CYP2D6.stat_label: estimated ultrarapid metabolizers in this region
CYP2D6.real_case: Documented in codeine: FDA Boxed Warning (Feb 2013) after pediatric deaths from ultrarapid conversion to morphine.
CYP2D6.relevant_drug_classes: Prodrugs activated by CYP2D6 — e.g. certain opioids, some antidepressants and antiarrhythmics

HLA-B_1502.label: HLA-B*15:02 (allele carrier)
HLA-B_1502.mechanism: Carriers of HLA-B*15:02 face a dramatically elevated risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis when exposed to drugs that trigger this immune response.
HLA-B_1502.stat_label: allele frequency in Han Chinese cohorts (Chung et al., 2004)
HLA-B_1502.real_case: Documented in carbamazepine: Chung et al., Nature (2004); Taiwan now mandates pre-prescription screening.
HLA-B_1502.relevant_drug_classes: Aromatic anticonvulsants and structurally related compounds (carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin class)

HLA-B_5701.label: HLA-B*57:01 (allele carrier)
HLA-B_5701.mechanism: Carriers of HLA-B*57:01 can develop severe, sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions to drugs that bind this allele's antigen-presentation site.
HLA-B_5701.stat_label: carrier frequency (CPIC pooled data) vs 1-6.7% in most other regions
HLA-B_5701.real_case: Documented in abacavir: PREDICT-1 trial, NEJM (2008) — screening cut reactions from 2.7% to 0%.
HLA-B_5701.relevant_drug_classes: Nucleoside analogue drugs metabolized/presented similarly to abacavir

CYP2C19.label: CYP2C19 (poor metabolizer)
CYP2C19.mechanism: Poor CYP2C19 metabolizers cannot efficiently activate prodrugs that require this enzyme, meaning the drug may simply fail to work at standard doses.
CYP2C19.stat_label: poor metabolizers documented in Vanuatu (Hsu et al., 2008)
CYP2C19.real_case: Documented in clopidogrel: FDA Boxed Warning (2010) on reduced effectiveness in poor metabolizers.
CYP2C19.relevant_drug_classes: Prodrugs activated by CYP2C19 — e.g. antiplatelets, some PPIs and antidepressants

VKORC1.label: VKORC1 (dose sensitivity)
VKORC1.mechanism: A common VKORC1 variant lowers the required dose for drugs targeting this pathway; using a standard Western starting dose risks overdose in patients carrying it.
VKORC1.stat_label: carry the dose-lowering variant in East Asian cohorts, vs ~39% in Europeans
VKORC1.real_case: Documented in warfarin: FDA label (2010) added genotype-based dosing table.
VKORC1.relevant_drug_classes: Vitamin K antagonists and other VKORC1-targeting anticoagulants

CYP2C9_AA.label: CYP2C9 cluster variant (African-ancestry-specific)
CYP2C9_AA.mechanism: A chromosome-10 CYP2C9-cluster variant common in African-ancestry populations was missed entirely by dosing algorithms built on European and Asian cohort data, causing systematic dose miscalibration.
CYP2C9_AA.stat_label: variant absent from algorithms trained on non-African-ancestry cohorts
CYP2C9_AA.real_case: Documented in warfarin: Perera et al., The Lancet (2013) — genome-wide study found the missed variant.
CYP2C9_AA.relevant_drug_classes: Any drug whose dosing algorithm was trained predominantly on European/Asian pharmacogenomic cohorts

NAT2.label: NAT2 (slow acetylator)
NAT2.mechanism: Slow NAT2 acetylators break down NAT2-dependent drugs more slowly, letting toxic intermediate metabolites accumulate and raising liver-injury risk.
NAT2.stat_label: slow-acetylator genotype frequency in an Indian TB patient cohort (2024 study)
NAT2.real_case: Documented in isoniazid: National Medical Journal of India (2013); Monaldi Archives (2024).
NAT2.relevant_drug_classes: NAT2-metabolized drugs — e.g. antituberculars, some sulfonamides and hydralazine-class drugs
